I understand that in the EU and many other countries, an e-bike must stop assisting at 25\u00A0km/h. Above that, it may legally be a moped that needs approval, registration, insurance, a licence and a helmet.
I will use settings above 25\u00A0km/h only where it is legal, for example on private land.
I understand that higher speeds increase the risk of accidents, injury and damage, and that I am solely responsible.
I understand that changing the speed limit may void my warranty and affect my insurance.
I understand that this app is unofficial and not affiliated with ENGWE. It is provided “as is”, without warranty or liability (GPL-3.0, sections 15 and 16), and I use it at my own risk.

Legal & safety
You accepted these statements on %1$s (text version %2$d).
Tested on one bike and firmware only

Speed changes have been tested only on the ENGWE E26 3.0 Pro with IoT firmware 218CAN. In those tests the limit went back to 25\u00A0km/h when the bike was switched off. On other models or firmware, a change might behave differently and could be permanent. Tap 25 when you’re done.
You can check your bike’s IoT firmware version in the ENGWE app.
